track.title: Bayat-e Esfahan
track.notes: Tagged title: Esfahan. Same audio as 'Ahmad Ebadi, Setar Solo' (2000), CD1 track 6 (Bayat-e Esfahan), sample-aligned; that release is not analysed separately.

just_intervals.note: measured octave minus 1200 ¢, register to register

progression.narrative: The performance opens on F4 and dwells most on F in Phrase 1. Phrase 5 (1:18.5) introduces Ak, Bb, centred on G. Phrase 7 (1:48.7) introduces C, centred on G. The line peaks at C5 (571.1 Hz) at 2:27.8. It closes on G4, not the tonic (C5 → Bb4 → Ak4 → Bb4 → G4 → G4).

theory_fit.name: Farhat interval classes
theory_fit.description: Interval classes Hormoz Farhat measured in performance practice ("The Dastgah Concept in Persian Music", 1990). Approximate centres.

flags: tonic F set in the catalog (Bayat-e Esfahan's finalis, about F# +25 cents (187.7 Hz): the pitch set fits Bayat-e Esfahan best from it, at the position of his Lord of Setar Bayat-e Esfahan (185-187 Hz), named F there to stay a 4th above his Homayoun on C. The vote picked the 3rd above. Inference, not yet by ear); the runs' vote favoured 445.2 Hz (A)
